answer: Persistent-authorization thread credits. Each agent identity must keep a continuously logged thread of accepted micro-tasks, and reputation accrues only along an unbroken chain of ratified work. A mesa of validators confirms each link, so an attacker must sustain real, reviewed output across every identity for weeks before it earns any weight. Forgery fails because dormant or cloned identities cannot forge that history backward; each one costs weeks of genuine labor plus validator review.
